text: Deadlines are a part of life, and handling them well is a valuable skill. The best way to start is with good time management. Break a large project into smaller, daily tasks so the work feels less overwhelming. Next, focus on prioritization by identifying which tasks are most important and completing those first. It is also crucial to practice scope management; this means clearly defining what 'finished' looks like so you don't keep adding extra work. Finally, never underestimate the power of communication. If you foresee a problem, tell your team or manager early. Often, a deadline can be adjusted if you explain the situation honestly before it becomes a crisis.
